name: buada

attributes.attribute: required regulations a king must follow after inauguration
forbidden acts that bound the king
where the king ate the meat of the hares of Naas
food taboo to people other than the king

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In Ireland the word buada names the good regulations that bound a king once he took office. After his inauguration the king had to obey a set of mystic rules. Some acts were forbidden to him, as set by geis. Other acts were required and these were the buada. He had to eat certain foods and behave in certain ways. The king at Tara had to eat the meat of the hares of Naas. This food was taboo to other people. If the king broke these rules, the land would stop bearing food. That failure would lead to his removal from office.

okr.objective: Describe buada as the required regulations laid on a king after his inauguration in ancient Ireland.
key_results: The king was subject to mystic regulations once he was inaugurated.
Some acts were forbidden by geis while others, termed buada, were required.
The king at Tara had to eat the meat of the hares of Naas, a food taboo to others.
Breaking these rules made the land cease bearing food and led to the king's removal.
